text: In the seen there will be just the seen... Then you will not be by it. And when you are not by it, you are not in it. And when you are not in it, you are neither here nor there nor in between. This itself is the end of suffering.
plain: In the seen there will be just the seen... Then you will not be by it. And when you are not by it, you are not in it. And when you are not in it, you are neither here nor there nor in between. This itself is the end of suffering.

text: Herein, Ananda, a monk is thus conscious: 'This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.'

say: Herein, Ananda, a monk is thus conscious — 'This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely, everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the wanting ends, nothing pulls you any more, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel.'

text: Dhono na hi tena manñati yadidam ditthasutam mutesu va — the arahant does not imagine 'thereby', namely by whatever is seen, heard and sensed.

say: the arahant does not imagine 'thereby', namely, by whatever is seen, heard and sensed.

text:
With the idea of sharpening the razor, if one grabs it tightly and
rubs it on the sharpening stone, it will only become blunt. Paramasana,
grasping, grabbing, is something like that.

say: With the idea of sharpening the razor, if one grabs it tightly and rubs it on the sharpening stone, it will only become blunt. Paramasana, holding on, grabbing, is something like that.

text:
What tranquillity meditation does, is to temporarily calm them down and
derive some sort of happiness. That too is necessary from the point of
view of concentration, to do away with restlessness and the like, but
it does not dispel ignorance. That is why, in insight meditation, one
tries to understand preparations for what they are by dispelling
ignorance. The more one sees preparations as preparations, ignorance is
dispelled, and the more one dispels ignorance, the preparations lose
their significance as preparations.

say: What tranquillity meditation does, is to temporarily calm them down and derive some sort of happiness. That too is necessary from the point of view of concentration, to do away with restlessness and the like, but it does not dispel not seeing how it works. That is why, in insight meditation, one tries to understand things the mind makes for what they are by dispelling not seeing how it works. The more one sees things the mind makes as things the mind makes, not seeing how it works is dispelled, and the more one dispels not seeing how it works, the things the mind makes lose their significance as things the mind makes.

text:
It is said that the wandering ascetic Upatissa was able to arouse the
path of Stream-winning on hearing just the first two lines.

say: It is said that the wandering ascetic Upatissa was able to arouse the path of Stream-winning on hearing just the first two lines.

text:
When walking, he understands: 'I am walking'; when standing, he
understands: 'I am standing'; when sitting, he understands: 'I am
sitting'; when lying down, he understands: 'I am lying down'. While
keeping one's postures in this manner, one sees in outline one's own
form as if one were acting in a monodrama.

say: When walking, he understands — 'I am walking', when standing, he understands — 'I am standing', when sitting, he understands — 'I am sitting', when lying down, he understands — 'I am lying down'. While keeping one's postures in this manner, one sees in outline one's own form as if one were acting in a monodrama.

text:
First: up, up, up, then: down, down, down, and then: up down, up down,
up down. The third combined movement ensures that those parts of the
blade still untouched by the stone will also get duly sharpened.

say: The third combined movement ensures that those parts of the blade still untouched by the stone will also get duly sharpened.

text:
The purpose is the breaking up of the foundation for cravings,
conceits and views. For 'me' to acquire some object out of craving
that object has to exist apart from 'me'... The statement 'this is
mine' presupposes a duality between 'me' and 'mine'.

say: The purpose is the breaking up of the foundation for cravings, conceits and views. For 'me' to acquire some object out of craving that object has to exist apart from 'me'... The statement 'this is mine' presupposes a duality between 'me' and 'mine'.

text:
First of all one has to mindfully scan or scrutinize it... But based
on that scrutiny, the four right endeavours play their role in regard
to unskilful and skilful mental states.

say: First of all one has to mindfully scan or scrutinize it... But based on that scrutiny, the four right endeavours play their role in regard to unskilful and skilful mental states.

text:
These seven tool-kits are interconnected. From the satipaṭṭhāna
tool-kit, the sammappadhāna tool-kit comes out as a matter of course.

say: These seven tool-kits are interconnected. From the satipatthana — four ways of paying attention — tool-kit, the sammappadhana tool-kit comes out as a matter of course.

text: One arouses a longing for the supreme deliverances thus: 'When shall I enter upon and abide in that sphere that the Noble Ones now enter upon and abide in?' In one who arouses such a longing... unhappiness arises conditioned by that longing.

say: One arouses a longing for the supreme deliverances thus — 'When shall I enter upon and abide in that sphere that the Noble Ones now enter upon and abide in?' In one who arouses such a longing... unhappiness arises conditioned by that longing.

text:
Just as a blue lotus, born in the water, rises well above the water
and remains unsmeared — so the Tathagata dwells detached from ten
things with a mind unrestricted.

say: Just as a blue lotus, born in the water, rises well above the water and remains unsmeared — so the Tathagata dwells detached from ten things with a mind unrestricted.

text:
One comes to know one's strongpoint, where one's forte lies...
One might recognize chanda, desire or interest, as one's strongpoint...
Another might discover that his true personality emerges in the thick
of striving... One who belongs to the wisdom category is never tired of
investigation.

say: One comes to know one's strongpoint, where one's forte lies... One might recognize chanda, desire or interest, as one's strongpoint... Another might discover that his true personality emerges in the thick of striving... One who belongs to the wisdom category is never tired of investigation.
